hints.title: Finite State Cycle Detection
hints.text: With only 8 cells and the outer two fixed at 0 after day 1, there are at most 2^6 = 64 distinct states. The sequence must repeat in a cycle.

hints.title: Fast-Forwarding Modulo Period
hints.text: Record the day each state was first observed in a lookup map. Once a repeated state is found, skip full periods using modulo arithmetic.

hints.title: Bitmask or Tuple Simulation
hints.text: Convert state to tuple. While n > 0: if state in seen, cycle = seen[state] - n, n %= cycle; else seen[state] = n. If n > 0, decrement n and compute next_state where next[i] = 1 if state[i - 1] == state[i + 1] else 0.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating N up to 10^9 days one day at a time triggers Time Limit Exceeded.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Cycle detection finds the period in at most 14 steps, requiring negligible O(1) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should quickly calculate the maximum possible states (2^6 = 64) and implement cycle detection with modulo reduction.
complexity.notes: Cells 0 and 7 always become 0 starting from day 1.
